title: Rental replacement by-law to protect tenants
subtitle: Also: Lived Expertise Working Group extension, Jansen Avenue rezoning, Ottawa Street North condominium; Mill Street item deferred.
overview: The committee's main business was a Rental Replacement By-law. It would apply when a property with six or more rental units is demolished or converted. The committee recommended the by-law, a related Official Plan amendment and changes to the demolition control by-law {{vote:m4}}. It also asked staff to report back in June 2025 on how the by-law is working and on renovation-eviction by-laws elsewhere in Ontario. An amendment to widen the definition of a comparable replacement unit was defeated {{vote:m5}}.

The committee also recommended extending the Lived Expertise Working Group pilot to June 2026, rezoning 179 Jansen Avenue, and draft approval of a vacant land condominium at 20 Ottawa Street North. A condominium application for 455-509 Mill Street was removed from the agenda at the applicant's request. It is expected back in August 2024.

These are recommendations. Council must still adopt or change them, and the Official Plan amendment goes to the Region of Waterloo for approval. Council was expected to take up the rental replacement item at its June 24 meeting.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended the by-law, an Official Plan amendment sent to the Region of Waterloo, and changes to the demolition control by-law, with staff to keep working on a tenant assistance policy and report back in June 2025 {{vote:m4}}.
An amendment to define a comparable replacement unit by rooms generally equal to the size of the displaced tenant's unit was defeated {{vote:m5}}.
The committee recommended extending the pilot to June 2026, staffed by the City, to support the Housing for All Strategy and the Official Plan project.
The committee recommended approving the zoning by-law amendment for 179 Jansen Avenue as set out in the staff report.
The committee recommended draft approval of the vacant land condominium plan at 20 Ottawa Street North, subject to the staff report's conditions.

debate: Delegates in support asked for improvements: a defined affordable rent (some suggested the CMHC definition), former tenants returning at the rent they paid before, and a longer or no limit on the 10-year affordability period.
A legal clinic delegate said the by-law places the duty to notify tenants on the developer and asked that the City do it instead. The delegate also asked for a clear way to enforce tenant rights.

Staff said the by-law is meant to rebalance development: it steers redevelopment toward sites without tenants and requires replacement of displaced units. It cannot cover renovation evictions. Staff said three past applications in the last 5 to 10 years would have been affected.

Some councillors said the by-law could slow general housing supply and wanted to monitor it. Others said it is a limited tool and that senior governments need to act. Councillors also asked about offering tenants a nearby off-site unit, which staff said they could look into.

On the comparable-unit amendment, staff said the City lacks legal authority to require specific unit sizes or bedroom counts. They noted tenants can choose among three options: a temporary replacement unit, a rent waiver or a cash payout.
